Handover careful habits for cabin readiness
This section covers the routine in plain words

Cabin Readiness and Animal Transfer

The Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps a steady hand on all routine animal travel steps so the cabin team, the ground team, and the desk share the same practical picture. We check each booking record for clear care notes, confirm that carrier details match the travel file, and pass forward any handling limits that affect movement through the airport or placement in the cabin. When a traveler arrives with a pet, the desk staff use calm language, repeat the key points in simple words, and make sure the carrier remains secure, clean, and ready for the next handoff.

If a carrier shows signs of stress, damage, or poor airflow, the desk pauses the move and alerts the duty contact before the animal is released for further processing. Any change in route, cabin plan, or special care instruction is shared with the crew in a direct handover note so the cabin team can continue observation without confusion. The ground team must keep carriers upright, avoid unnecessary handling, and maintain a quiet flow between check-in, screening, and boarding. Staff should never leave an animal without a responsible handover, and they should always confirm that the paperwork, labels, and visible identification are in line with the booking.

When a traveler asks for assistance, the desk offers clear next steps and avoids making promises that the operation cannot support. If the pet appears unwell, agitated, or unable to travel safely, the desk follows the escalation path and records the concern in the service log. The same careful process applies whether the movement is routine or sensitive, because steady practice protects the animal and helps the crew do the right thing at the right moment. This calm routine supports a reliable cabin handover and keeps service consistent across the day.

For any doubtful case, contact the duty supervisor through the normal desk channel.
